## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kāyanibbindajātaka* (Ja 293), rendered in English as *Dispassion for the Body*, is a canonical narrative in the Pali Jātaka collection. The framing story (*nidāna*) is situated at the Jetavana monastery, where the Buddha delivered the teaching concerning a man afflicted with jaundice who had been given up by his physicians as incurable. In early modern scholarship, the critical apparatus to V. Fausböll’s edition records the manuscript reading *kayanibbinda-* [Fausböll 1879], while the index volume cross-references *Kayanibbinda-jātaka* to the form *Kāyavicchinda-* [Fausböll 1897].

 Computational analysis by DharmaNexus indicates Pali-internal text reuse between segments of the jātaka (§1.1–3.4) and both the commentary (*Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*) and the *Visuddhimagga* (§326_5–334) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matching, DharmaNexus also identifies an automated textual alignment with the Tibetan *Suvarṇavarṇāvadāna* (D4144) [DharmaNexus].
